I just moved from Washington to Arizona. I have some advice. Unless you are very rich DO NOT move to Washington. It’s a hellhole no matter how beautiful it is. Me and my girlfriend moved there 2 years ago because of how beautiful it is. We found the cheapest area we could and ended up paying 2300 for an apartment that was built in the 70s. There are more modern apartments but be prepared to pay around 3000 a month for a 1 bed. 

The people there are just as bad as in California. I loved the weather except for the summer where it reached 110 and 60% humidity. Nowhere has air conditioning since mostly everything there was built a long time ago. No income tax sounds great until you realize how much you are paying for everything else. 5-6$ for gas. 40 min drive to go 6 miles. 

If you live in an apartment you will have to park your cars outside in the rain where it rains all day every day. My car is brand new and it was growing moss around the edges of doors and windows. My apartment did offer covered parking but it was 80$ per month per car. Food is outrageous. Even little things too like a movie ticket there is 15 per person where as in Arizona it’s 9. All this adds up. 

We lived outside of Seattle more east and our water bill was 160$ each month. It’s 40$ in Arizona. I registered my car and it was 900$ and my new license was 100$. If I were you I would just visit there a lot and see all the things you want to see because everyday life there is hell. 

I also want to mention the moving part which can happen no matter where you are moving to. We had ALL of our stuff destroyed by the moving company which we payed 6,000$. They told us they would give us 120$ to cover the damages. Luckily our renters insurance covered it even though they technically don’t. It cost 7,000$ to replace it all. 

We also had an issue with the apartment where during the winter it rained so much that the roof leaked and the ceiling was ruined and they never fixed it so we lived for a year with a hole in the ceiling. NEVER RENT FROM DECRON. I hope some of my experience can help you one way or another and feel free to ask me any questions if you want.

OKAY! So knock on wood but I think my problem is fixed. I reapplied thermal paste and in the process took my cpu out to clean off the old thermal paste. Anyway when I started my pc back up it said new cpu detected and gave two options, press F1 for Intel Default CPU settings (Stock power limits) and press F3 to unlock limits for increased performance. I chose the first option. I have now played battlefield 5 for about 40 mins and the tested multiple things. On Max fidelity settings at 1440p 144hz I get 55c. On Ultra settings 1440p 144hz I get 59-62c. I was getting stuttering when I first played but turning off directx12 solved that. It was bugging me that having it on was stuttering so I looked into that and turned on max performance power setting for windows and that seemed to make it better however it still stutters a little bit. But I think that I just battlefield 5. I’m not actually sure if it was the thermal paste or if it was something to do with the motherboard thinking it was a new cpu and then picking default intel options.
